france24fr.description: C’est en réponse à une demande de Téhéran que Donald Trump a signé le protocole d’accord mercredi soir à Versailles et que la Maison Blanche a publié la vidéo sur ses réseaux sociaux, selon notre correspondant en Iran. Les responsables iraniens tenaient particulièrement à ce que le protocole d'accord soit rédigé en anglais et en persan.

france24fr.title: L'Égypte face à l'addiction du "gaming"
france24fr.description: Dans les rues du Caire, les cafés et les espaces de “gaming” font désormais partie du paysage, particulièrement dans les quartiers populaires. Les Égyptiens passent en moyenne 1h43 par jour à jouer, dépassant toutes les autres nations. 43,5 % des joueurs mineurs en Égypte sont considérés comme dépendants. En février, l’Etat a lancé une campagne de lutte contre cette addiction. Reportage de Mathilde Delvigne.

france24fr.title: Législative partielle à haut risque pour Keir Starmer challengé par Andy Burnham
france24fr.description: Les bureaux de vote ont ouvert jeudi à Makerfield, dans le nord-ouest de l'Angleterre, pour une élection législative qui pourrait marquer le début de la fin pour Keir Starmer : son principal rival au Labour, Andy Burnham, espère s'y faire élire député, avec l'ambition d'évincer le Premier ministre de Downing Street.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Mbappé fait taire les critiques ?
france24fr.description: Auteur de 2 des 3 buts de l'équipe de France pour sa victoire face au Sénégal à l'entame de la Coupe du Monde, Kylian Mbappé fait taire les critiques.

france24fr.title: G7 : le pari d'Emmanuel Macron
france24fr.description: En invitant Donald Trump à Versailles pour un dîner en l'honneur des 250 ans de l'indépendance des Etats-Unis mercredi soir, Emmanuel Macron fait le pari que le président américain assistera à l'intégralité du G7 à Evian et validera les choix de ses partenaires. Pari gagnant ? On va plus loin avec Niagalé Bagayoko et Antoine Mariotti.

france24fr.title: France Médias Monde à VivaTech 2026 : IA et médias, drones, villes et changement climatique
france24fr.description: Pour les dix ans du salon VivaTech, ‪France Médias Monde déploie un dispositif inédit au cœur de l'événement et une programmation exceptionnelle. À suivre sur YouTube lors de cette deuxième journée de salon, jeudi : un débat sur les drones et leur financement, une table ronde sur les médias et les plateformes d'intelligence artificielle, mais aussi une émission sur les innovations visant à rendre les villes plus résilientes face au réchauffement climatique.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Colombie assure, premier but en Coupe du monde pour l’Ouzbékistan
france24fr.description: La Colombie s’est imposée sur le score de 3-1 face à l’Ouzbékistan à Mexico grâce à un Luis Diaz étincelant. Pour sa première en Coupe du monde, le pays d’Asie centrale a tenté d’imposer son jeu et a été récompensé par un but.

france24fr.title: Niger : des coups de feu entendus à l'aéroport de Niamey
france24fr.description: Des coups de feu ont éclaté tôt jeudi matin à l'aéroport de Niamey, la capitale du Niger, ont indiqué des habitants à l'AFP, plusieurs mois après une attaque jihadiste de grande ampleur perpétrée dans ce même complexe.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Harry Kane en majesté, Ronaldo contesté
france24fr.description: Certains ont séduit, plusieurs ont déçu, et d'autres ont créé la surprise dans un premier tour de phase de groupe animé de la Coupe du Monde 2026. Avec son succès face à la Croatie (4-2), l'Angleterre a réitéré ses ambitions de remporter ce titre qui leur échappe depuis 1966, tandis que le Portugal, considéré parmi les favoris de la compétition, a été tenu en échec face a la tenace RD Congo.

france24fr.title: Gazoduc transsaharien : un rêve africain qui pourrait bouleverser l'équilibre énergétique mondial
france24fr.description: Après deux décennies de reports, le projet pharaonique de gazoduc transsaharien, visant à exporter le gaz nigérian vers l'Europe via le Niger et l'Algérie, est revenu sur le devant de la scène avec l'annonce du lancement, début juin, des travaux de construction sur le tronçon algérien. Dans quelle mesure ce gazoduc peut-il redessiner la carte du gaz entre l'Afrique et l'Europe ? France 24 fait le point.

france24fr.title: Déficit commercial européen : "La Chine, c'est Voldemort"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce jeudi 18 juin, la réunion, aujourd’hui et demain, des dirigeants de l’UE à Bruxelles, pour tenter de réduire les déséquilibres commerciaux avec la Chine, dont la puissance grandissante inquiète aussi les Etats-Unis et le Japon. Le vote, hier, au Parlement européen, autorisant une nouvelle génération d’OGM. Des nouvelles, également, du Mondial. Et la question du déboutonnage des chemises d’homme par forte chaleur... Un débat velu.

france24fr.title: Les présidents américain et iranien signent le protocole d'accord à distance
france24fr.description: Depuis le château de Versailles, Donald Trump a signé, mercredi soir, le protocole d'accord avec l'Iran, dans lequel Téhéran s'engage à rouvrir immédiatement le détroit d'Ormuz et, dans le cadre de futures négociations, à diluer son uranium enrichi en échange de la levée des sanctions internationales. Le document a été ratifié dans la foulée par son homologue iranien Massoud Pezeshkian.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : l'Angleterre séduit pour son entrée, le Portugal patine
france24fr.description: Opposée à la Croatie, finaliste en 2018, l'Angleterre l'emporte (4-2), grâce notamment à un doublé de Harry Kane. L'attaquant anglais rejoint Gary Lineker comme meilleur buteur anglais à la Coupe du monde.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: La RD Congo tient tête au Portugal, l'Angleterre séduit et l'Ouzbékistan marque son premier but en Coupe du monde... Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Signature du protocole d'accord : une première étape vers une sortie du conflit
france24fr.description: La signature du protocole d'accord entre les États-Unis et l'Iran n'est une première étape vers la fin du conflit, rappelle le correspondant de France 24 à Washington, Matthieu Mabin, car les deux pays "reviennent de loin" après trois mois et demi d'"un face à face "extrêmement dangereux".

zeit.title: Sibel Kekilli: »In mich wurde viel Gift geschüttet«
zeit.description: Die Schauspielerin Sibel Kekilli erlebte in ihrer Familie jahrelang Gewalt. Hier spricht sie erstmals darüber, was das mit ihrem Leben gemacht hat.

zeit.title: Gesundheit: Lungenkrebs-Fälle in Hessen stark gestiegen
Neuling aus dem Saarland: «Lichtjahre voraus»: Wie sich Elversberg behaupten will
Gewerkschaft: IG Metall sieht sich nach Betriebsratswahlen im Aufwind
Polizeieinsatz: Totes Kleinkind in Auto – Obduktion soll Todesursache klären
Lage im Überblick: Vermittler Pakistan: Abkommen USA-Iran tritt in Kraft
Reformen: Wochenarbeitszeit statt Achtstundentag? Entwurf liegt vor
Sommerliches Wetter: Bis zu 38 Grad erwartet: Heiße Tage und schwere Gewitter
Finanzpolitik: Rechnungshof weist auf Risiken sächsischer Finanzpolitik hin
Arbeitszeitgesetz: Bundesarbeitsministerin plant Pflicht zur Arbeitszeiterfassung
zeit.description: Bärbel Bas will die Wochenarbeitszeiten flexibilisieren – dann wären Arbeitstage mit mehr als acht Stunden möglich. Auch strengere Dokumentationspflichten könnten kommen.

zeit.title: Arbeitslosigkeit: Arbeiten trotz Absagen
zeit.description: Wer monatelang keinen Job findet, hinterfragt seine Ausbildung, seine Träume, sein Leben. Zehn Ideen gegen die Verzweiflung, von Grabreden bis Erdbeerverkauf.

zeit.title: Smashed Chicken Burger: Der Sommer zwischen zwei Brötchen
zeit.description: Dieser Smashburger aus Hühnchen mit eingelegten Zwiebeln und Harissa schreit nach Grillparty. Dabei brauchen Sie gar keine Kohle: Eine schwere Pfanne tut es auch!

zeit.title: Großbritannien: Uralte Robin-Hood-Eiche in Nottingham abgestorben
zeit.description: In England ist eine über tausend Jahre alte Eiche gestorben, die in der Robin-Hood-Legende eine Rolle spielt. Die vielen Besucher sollen dafür mitverantwortlich sein.

zeit.title: Nato: Hegseth kündigt weitere Überprüfung der US-Truppenpräsenz in Europa an
zeit.description: US-Verteidigungsminister Pete Hegseth will die Truppenstärke in Europa erneut prüfen. Nato-Generalsekretär Mark Rutte fordert die Europäer auf, sich mehr zu engagieren.

zeit.title: Irankrieg: Deutsche Marine auf dem Weg zu möglichem Einsatz in Straße von Hormus
zeit.description: Zwei Marineschiffe sind unterwegs nach Dschibuti. Die Bundesregierung will bei Bedarf für den Schutz der Schifffahrt in der Straße von Hormus bereit sein. Das Liveblog

nzz.title: Rekorde, Familiengeschichten und ein Erpel als Maskottchen: die zehn denkwürdigsten Momente der ersten WM-Woche
nzz.description: Die Weltmeisterschaft sorgt auf und neben dem Platz für Schlagzeilen. Wir haben die aussergewöhnlichsten gesammelt.

nzz.title: Dramatischer Crash in Texas: Passanten retten fünf Menschen aus brennendem Business-Jet
nzz.description: Ein Cessna-Absturz in Texas fordert ein Todesopfer. Der Unfall reiht sich ein in eine Serie von Unglücken mit den beliebten Citation-Business-Jets.

nzz.title: Ein polnischer Tiergarten-Mord? Nach der Tötung eines kremlkritischen Künstlers steht der russische Geheimdienst im Verdacht
nzz.description: Der russische Künstler Semjon Skrepezki war ein ätzender Kritiker des Kremls und des russischen Nationalismus. Seine Ermordung im polnischen Exil wirft Fragen auf.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Ukrainische Drohnen treffen Raffinerie in Moskau +++ Selenski spricht mit Trump und Macron
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: Der Ebola-Ausbruch in Kongo verschärft sich: was hinter der seltenen Bundibugyo-Variante steckt
nzz.description: Karten und Grafiken zeigen, wie sich das Virus alarmierend schnell verbreitet und wer besonders betroffen ist.

nzz.title: Das AKW-Verbot fällt: Der Nationalrat unterstützt Bundesrat Rösti nun doch
nzz.description: Eine knappe Mehrheit reicht: Der Nationalrat schliesst sich dem Ständerat an und widerruft damit seinen Entscheid vom Montag.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Deutschland: Konjunkturaussichten leicht verbessert +++ Wadephul will polnische Opfer des Nationalsozialismus entschädigen +++ Totes Kleinkind im Auto
KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Mehrheit der Bevölkerung für strengere Kapitalauflagen für UBS
Glanz und Elend der Guten Dienste: wie die Schweiz seit Jahrzehnten zwischen Iran und den USA vermittelt – bei allen Turbulenzen
nzz.description: Am Freitag soll es auf dem Bürgenstock zu einem grossen Moment kommen. Oder doch nicht? Eine kurze Geschichte über den mühseligen Dienst der helvetischen Diplomatie.

nzz.title: Messi spielt sich in den Fussball-Olymp – Ronaldo bleibt gegen Kongo-Kinshasa ungefährlich
nzz.description: Der Argentinier bleibt der Massstab im Fussball: Per Hattrick stellt er den WM-Torrekord ein. Sein alter Rivale kann nicht mithalten – und bewahrt Portugal nicht vor einer Blamage.

nzz.title: Die Schweizerische Nationalbank bleibt den Nullzinsen treu – und folgt nicht der Zinswende anderer Zentralbanken
nzz.description: Die Inflation ist durch den Iran-Krieg zwar auch in der Schweiz gestiegen. Sie liegt aber immer noch auf einem tiefen Niveau. Die SNB ist weiterhin bereit, «bei Bedarf» am Devisenmarkt zu intervenieren, sollte der Franken rasch und übermässig erstarken.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Sprit- und Gaspreise deutlich gesunken – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Bist du müde? Warum spielst du mit diesen Schuhen? Warum trägst du kein Tape?»: Was der Arzt der Schweizer Nationalmannschaft von den Spielern wissen will
nzz.description: Der Sportmediziner Philippe Tscholl tut alles dafür, dass sich die Schweizer Fussballspieler nicht verletzen. Er hat aber auch Tipps für Hobbysportler und sagt, in welchem Alter man besser aufhören sollten, zu kicken.

nzz.title: Die Schweiz und Deutschland fallen bei der globalen Wettbewerbsfähigkeit zurück. Doch zwischen den Ländern liegen Welten
nzz.description: Im globalen Vergleich gehört die Schweiz zu den konkurrenzfähigsten Standorten der Welt, für Deutschland gilt das immer weniger. Doch jetzt zeigt auch die Eidgenossenschaft eine Schwäche. Beim Kriterium «wirtschaftliche Leistungsfähigkeit» ist das Land abgestürzt.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Schweizer Aussendepartement rechnet weiterhin mit Treffen auf dem Bürgenstock +++ Rahmenabkommen von Iran und den USA unterzeichnet
nzz.description: Zwischen den USA und Iran herrscht seit Februar 2026 Krieg, die Folgen sind weltweit spürbar. Nun scheint sich ein Ende des Konflikts anzubahnen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

observador.title: Ormuz será reaberto "instantaneamente", garante Paquistão
observador.description: Memorando assinado em Versalhes "entrará em vigor com efeito imediato": levantamento das operações militares em todas as frentes, passagem por Ormuz e compromisso iraniano com programa nuclear.

observador.title: Álvaro Magalhães: "Cristiano Ronaldo deve retirar-se"
observador.description: Álvaro Magalhães considera que CR7 deve sair em beleza, para não manchar a carreira. O antigo jogador critica falta de entrega da seleção: sucesso nos clubes "adormece" desejo de vencer pelo país.

observador.title: 10h. PS volta a propor Luísa Neto para provedora de justiça
observador.description: PS e PSD querem que votação decorra no dia 3 de julho. Ainda neste jornal, Governo e Chega admitem negociar a lei laboral até depois do inicio do debate no Parlamento.

observador.title: "Widow's Bay": um tesouro de ilha
observador.description: Dois ingredientes fazem da série da Apple TV+ uma das melhores produções de 2026: o perfeito cruzamento entre comédia e mistério (e algum terror); e o elenco, liderado por Matthew Rhys.

observador.title: PJ investiga morte de criança de 8 anos em Valpaços
observador.description: A Polícia Judiciária está a investigar o caso de uma criança de 8 anos encontrada morta quarta-feira, no concelho de Valpaços, depois do alerta para o seu desaparecimento, avançaram fontes policiais.

observador.title: Fonte da Telha espera melhorias no acesso à praia
observador.description: O inverno rigoroso e o mar alteraram o areal da Fonte da Telha e obrigaram a investimentos privados. Agora, os concessionários esperam que o novo plano de estacionamento devolva ordem à praia.

observador.title: Portugal é só ratinhos na roda a trabalhar para aquecer?
observador.description: Com a produtividade no fundo, Portugal continua a ter poucos resultados. Entre tachos e reformas no banco, o país imita a seleção: muito passe lateral, mas o golo nunca chega.

observador.title: O milagre do treinador norueguês que morreu sete minutos
observador.description: Quando Solbakken ainda era jogador, o seu coração esteve parado 7 minutos. O incidente precipitou o fim da sua carreira como atleta, mas abriu caminho para o atual cargo de treinador.

observador.title: As propostas do Chega para alterar a reforma laboral
observador.description: Pela boca de Montenegro, o Governo mostrou-se disponível para aceitar algumas das propostas de alteração do Chega à reforma laboral. Uma delas prevê nova licença para avós ficarem com netos pequenos.

observador.title: Acidente na A5 condiciona trânsito no sentido Cascais-Lisboa
observador.description: Colisão entre dois carros, na zona de Queijas, provocou uma vítima com ferimentos leves e cortou a via da esquerda, no sentido Cascais-Lisboa.

observador.title: 9h. Israel volta a atacar o Líbano
observador.description: O Irão já tinha avisado que iria considerar qualquer ataque israelita no Líbano uma violação do memorando de entendimento. Ainda, 15 concelhos de seis distritos estão sob perigo máximo de incêndio.

observador.title: Mundial. Arranca a segunda jornada da fase de grupos
observador.description: Na ressaca do empate de Portugal com a RD Congo, seleções voltam a entrar em campo para a segunda jornada. Hoje há Chéquia-África do Sul, Suíça-Bósnia, Canadá-Qatar e México-Coreia do Sul.

observador.title: Hoje tenho mais cromos da bola para a troca
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro (que parece recusar a baixa da idade da reforma), o governo (que esteve no Mundial) e os patrioteiros da bola (que abundam na política) são o Bom, o Mau e o Vilão.

observador.title: Portugal no Mundial: muita parra, pouca uva e sem borga
observador.description: Entre nomes trocados e jogos que parecem brocas de dentista, a seleção falhou a borga no Solar dos Presuntos. Em Houston, encontrar um tuga é mais difícil que ganhar o Euromilhões.

observador.title: A política, o futebol e os equívocos de um mau casamento
observador.description: Os deputados já não vão aos jogos nos Estados Unidos mas não se pense que a política cortou relações com o futebol. Afinal de contas, faz quase 100 anos que tudo começou, na Itália de Benito Mussolini

observador.title: Números, notas e imagens de um empate que soube a derrota
observador.description: Seleção empata na estreia no Mundial. Governo substitui dirigentes da Segurança Social e PS fala em purga. Trump assinou em Paris memorando com o Irão. O perigo das noites tropicais.

observador.title: Seleção de luxo, mas futebol de chinelo: o flop na estreia
observador.description: Com craques de elite, Portugal jogou como se estivesse na praia. Ronaldo tocou menos na bola que o guarda-redes e Martínez parece que adormeceu no banco. A Seleção foi para o Mundial ou para a praia?

observador.title: 8h. Lei laboral. PS acusa PM de fazer "cambalhota política"
observador.description: José Luís Carneiro acusa Luís Montenegro de não rejeitar publicamente a discussão da descida da idade da reforma. Ainda, já foi assinado o memorando de entendimento entre Estados Unidos e Irão.

spiegel.title: Irankrieg: Das Abkommen zwischen den USA und Iran im Wortlaut
spiegel.description: USA und Iran haben ein Rahmenabkommen für ein Ende des Krieges unterzeichnet. Nun ist bekannt, worauf sich die Länder geeinigt haben – und was offen bleibt.

spiegel.title: Stonehenge: Archäologen finden möglichen Prototyp
spiegel.description: In der Nähe von Stonehenge haben Wissenschaftler Hinweise auf eine 5000 Jahre alte Holzkonstruktion entdeckt. Sie könnte der Vorläufer des berühmten Steinkreises sein. Darauf deutet die präzise Ausrichtung hin.

spiegel.title: BBC baut 550 Stellen ab: Sparprogramm von Matt Brittin, dem neuen Chef
spiegel.description: In Großbritannien steht der öffentliche Rundfunk unter Spardruck. Der neue BBC-Chef, Ex-Google-Manager Matt Brittin, kündigt nun einen Stellenabbau an. Auch traditionsreiche Sendungen werden gestrichen.

spiegel.title: Wirtschaft in Deutschland: Ifo-Institut hebt Konjunkturprognose leicht an
spiegel.description: Seit dem Morgen gilt offenbar das Rahmenabkommen zwischen den USA und Iran. Das belebt die Aussichten für die deutsche Wirtschaft ein wenig: Das Ifo-Institut prognostiziert 0,8 Prozent Wachstum.

spiegel.title: Wöchentliche Arbeitszeit: Tarifgebundene Firmen sollen Achtstundentag lockern können
spiegel.description: Ministerin Bärbel Bas will grundsätzlich am Achtstundentag festhalten. Tarifparteien sollen aber eine wöchentliche Höchstarbeitszeit vereinbaren können. Ein Verband spricht von »Arbeitsverweigerung«.

spiegel.title: Esther Sedlaczek über ihre Krise: »Ich habe mich immer selbst fertiggemacht«
spiegel.description: Esther Sedlaczek stieg rasant auf: von der RTL-Aushilfe zur WM-Moderatorin, der Millionen zuschauen, wenn sie mit Bastian Schweinsteiger fachsimpelt. Aber auf dem Weg musste sie durch eine tiefe Krise. Begegnung mit einer Frau, die sich befreit hat.

spiegel.title: Schorndorf: Tod von Kleinkind in Auto – Ermittlungen wegen fahrlässiger Tötung
spiegel.description: Die Staatsanwaltschaft Stuttgart ermittelt nach dem Tod eines kleinen Mädchens in einem Auto gegen die Mutter. Die 44-Jährige soll das Mädchen bei Hitze stundenlang in dem Fahrzeug vergessen haben.

spiegel.title: Archäologie: Pest tötete Menschen schon vor 5500 Jahren
spiegel.description: Im Mittelalter fielen der Pest in Europa Millionen Menschen zum Opfer. Doch schon lange vorher gab es tödliche Ausbrüche, wie eine neue Studie zeigt. Dabei starben besonders viele Kinder.

spiegel.title: Nato: US-Kürzungen gelten laut Mark Rutte ab sofort
spiegel.description: Angesichts der US-Pläne für die Nato mahnt Generalsekretär Rutte, dass Europa sich schneller um militärischen Ersatz kümmern müsse. Sorgen um die USA als Verbündete will er zerstreuen. Bei Pistorius ohne Erfolg.

spiegel.title: Olivia Wilde prangert Doppelstandards für ihr Liebesleben an
spiegel.description: Zu großer Altersunterschied! Viel zu schnell wieder jemand Neues! Die Beziehung zwischen Olivia Wilde und Harry Styles wurde hart kritisiert. Nun erzählt sie, wie es ihr erging, und vergleicht sich mit Ex-Partner Jason Sudeikis.

spiegel.title: Volkswagen: Susanne Wiegand tritt als VW-Aufsichtsrätin zurück
spiegel.description: Susanne Wiegand ist bisher die einzige unabhängige Aufsichtsrätin im Volkswagen-Konzern. Kurz vor ihrer geplanten Wahl schmeißt die Ex-Renk-Chefin ihr Amt hin. Eine Blamage für den größten deutschen Autobauer.

spiegel.title: Wiesbaden: 13-Jähriger auf E-Scooter stirbt nach Kollision mit Auto
spiegel.description: Er fuhr von einem Feldweg auf eine Landstraße und übersah dabei womöglich ein Auto: Ein Teenager ist in Wiesbaden tödlich verunglückt.

spiegel.title: Portraitbox: Hacker erbeuten Zehntausende Kinderfotos aus Schul-Webshop
spiegel.description: Kriminelle verschaffen sich Zugriff auf einen Clouddienst für Schul- und Kitafotografen – und kapern wohl Zehntausende Kinderbilder. Eltern sind wütend, Fotografen überfordert. Wie geht es nun weiter?

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Erling Haalands Tore lassen in Norwegen die Erde beben
spiegel.description: Norwegen nimmt erstmals seit 28 Jahren an einer WM teil. Der Auftaktsieg gegen Irak löste offenbar große Euphorie aus: Beim Doppelpack von Erling Haaland registrierten Seismologen in Bergen ein leichtes Erdbeben.

spiegel.title: Tübingen: Vermisster sechsjähriger Junge wohlbehalten gefunden
spiegel.description: Ein Sechsjähriger wurde seit Mittwochabend in Tübingen vermisst. Die Polizei bat bei der Suche nach dem Kind auch um Hinweise aus der Bevölkerung. Schließlich tauchte der Junge in Stuttgart auf.

spiegel.title: USA-Iran-Einigung: Trump verliert mit Iran-Politik Einfluss im Nahen Osten – Leitartikel von Dunja Ramadan
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident feiert sich für einen Deal, der auch ohne Irankrieg möglich gewesen wäre. Zurück bleiben arabische Staaten, die den Schaden haben – und ihre Zukunft nun ohne Washington organisieren.

spiegel.title: Straße von Hormus: Deutsche Marineschiffe passieren Suezkanalfür möglichen Minenräumeinsatz
spiegel.description: Um zügig in der Straße von Hormus einsatzbereit zu sein, schickt die Marine zwei Schiffe ins Rote Meer. Ob diese schließlich Minen räumen dürfen, hängt von vielen Faktoren ab.

spiegel.title: E-Mobilität: China verkauft mehr E-Autos als Verbrenner
spiegel.description: Die Mobilitätswende im größten Automarkt der Welt nimmt rasant zu: Wie das »Handelsblatt« berichtet, haben chinesische Stellen im April vorwiegend Elektroautos zugelassen.

letemps.title: La BNS maintient sa politique monétaire inchangée

register.title: Apple's WebKit performance tax leaves iOS browsers stuck in the slow lane, says Microsoft
register.description: Rival rendering engines could make pages load almost 30% faster on iPhones, Redmond claims

new-sci.title: Ancient monument may have been an early Stonehenge prototype
new-sci.description: Archaeologists have discovered traces of a wooden structure built 5000 years ago, 5 kilometres from Stonehenge, which appears to have been an even older monument for marking the summer solstice

new-sci.title: No young women have died of cervical cancer in England for years
new-sci.description: We already know the vaccine against human papillomavirus, or HPV, greatly reduces infections and cases of cervical cancer, and now we have the first evidence it prevents deaths too

new-sci.title: Chilling the body with drugs could limit brain damage from stroke
new-sci.description: Putting brain cells into a hibernation-like state via drugs that cool down core body temperature may help to preserve them following a stroke

new-sci.title: Oldest known plague outbreak killed hunter-gatherer children
new-sci.description: DNA evidence shows that plague bacteria devastated a community in Siberia more than 5000 years ago, challenging the idea that there were no major disease outbreaks before the advent of farming and large settlements

new-sci.title: Pigeons lock their eyes in place when they are flying
new-sci.description: Bird-mounted headsets and backpacks have revealed the surprising things pigeons do with their eyes when on the wing

new-sci.title: Our brains have their first thoughts surprisingly early in life
new-sci.description: By the time we’re born, our brains have all the hardware in place to form thoughts, and possibly even some conscious awareness

new-sci.title: Autism and ADHD are on the rise due to widening diagnostic criteria
new-sci.description: A study of 140,000 people suggests that a broadening of the diagnostic criteria for autism and ADHD explains the sharp rise in diagnoses, but that doesn't mean too many people are being told they are autistic or have ADHD

new-sci.title: Autism may have two distinct subtypes that vary by brain activity
new-sci.description: Evidence is mounting that there are distinct subtypes of autism, and now, scientists have found that the condition can vary according to the strength of people's brain connections

new-sci.title: The secrets to keeping your brain sharp in old age
new-sci.description: Neuroscientist Emily Rogalski studies superagers – people in their 80s or 90s with unusually keen memories, whose lifestyles suggest ways to slow cognitive decline

new-sci.title: A quantum state that lasts forever may finally be within our grasp
new-sci.description: Defying the laws of thermodynamics, experiments are beginning to show that a quantum state that is frozen forever might not be impossible. If we can tame it, it could unlock whole new types of matter

new-sci.title: Walking shark found in Papua New Guinea is new to science
new-sci.description: Hemiscyllium dudgeonae is the tenth recorded species of walking shark, which use their pectoral fins to move across reef flats, and its limited range means it may be at high risk of extinction

new-sci.title: Sperm have been made magnetic to allow IVF inside the body
new-sci.description: IVF could be done inside the body using a revolutionary technique that reduces the invasiveness of the traditional fertility treatment

new-sci.title: Arctic Ocean reaches tipping point that could be dire for marine life
new-sci.description: Disappearing sea ice is letting more sunlight in the Arctic Ocean and boosting phytoplankton growth, but this has depleted a crucial nutrient, which could severely affect animals higher up the food chain

new-sci.title: Technology is changing our perspective on nature – at every scale
new-sci.description: Inspired by Ariel Waldman’s docuseries Life Unearthed, columnist Annalee Newitz explores how microscopes, drones and specialised cameras are giving us an unprecedented view of nature from many different vantage points

new-sci.title: Has the answer to life's origins been hiding in our cells all along?
new-sci.description: The surprising discovery of mysterious blobs inside our cells is revolutionising our understanding of how life works, and how it got started

new-sci.title: The social media ban is an experiment – here’s how it will be studied
new-sci.description: Scientists have long grappled with how to measure the effect of social media on children. Now, the UK government has announced a total ban for everyone under 16, and researchers are rushing to design rigorous studies before it comes into effect

new-sci.title: Inside the start-up aiming for a giant leap in robot intelligence
new-sci.description: Physical Intelligence is drawing on the broad knowledge of large language models to help robots understand instructions and learn to carry out any task independently

new-sci.title: We may have finally solved cosmology's chicken-or-the-egg problem
new-sci.description: Galaxies and their supermassive black holes evolve together, but which came first is an ongoing question. Now we may finally have an answer, says columnist Leah Crane

phys-org.title: AI-driven optical tweezers sort hundreds of particles per hour without humans
phys-org.description: By teaching an AI to use optical tweezers, researchers from the University of Gothenburg and Chalmers University of Technology have sped up the analysis of life's smallest components. The AI platform captures particles, takes measurements and loads new samples, all without human intervention.

phys-org.title: How sea-ice microbes survive the Southern Ocean's harsh winter has implications for climate change
phys-org.description: A study led by South African scientists reveals that during winter, the sea ice around Antarctica harbors a reservoir of microbes, most of which have one thing in common—the ability to produce and break down a compound known to protect organisms in extreme environments.

phys-org.title: India learns to live with hotter summers
phys-org.description: On India's hot plains, scorching summers have become increasingly hard to endure, requiring adaptations and forcing life into the dark hours before the sun turns punishing.

phys-org.title: Bird flu kills 13,000 seal pups on remote Australian island
phys-org.description: A pathogenic strain of bird flu killed more than 13,000 elephant seal pups after infecting a breeding colony on a sub-Antarctic volcanic island, Australian scientists said Thursday.

phys-org.title: Tropical Cyclone Arthur weakens to a low pressure area along the upper Texas coast
phys-org.description: Tropical Storm Arthur was downgraded to a low pressure area along the upper Texas coast Wednesday night but forecasters expected its remnants to bring life-threatening flooding and days of heavy rains to parts of the southeastern United States, according to the National Hurricane Center in Miami.

phys-org.title: Tourism firms face complex path to sustainability
phys-org.description: Tourism businesses across Aotearoa New Zealand are working to become more sustainable, but a new study shows the process is complex and rarely straightforward. The research, based on in-depth interviews, data analysis and site visits with established tourism operators across the country, examines how businesses move from good intentions to more sustainable ways of working.

phys-org.title: Study analyzes buyers' assumptions about carpal chips in Thoroughbred yearlings
phys-org.description: See the vet reports during any yearling sale and you'll hear it—a ripple of concern when a veterinarian flags a bone chip on a radiograph of the horse's leg. Buyers often step away. Prices drop. The horse, in the minds of many, is already compromised. However, findings of a study from the University of Kentucky Maxwell H. Gluck Equine Research Center challenge that assumption, which carries real financial weight for sellers and consignors.

phys-org.title: New study maps the peanut genome in its entirety
phys-org.description: Peanuts are an important staple crop for many people around the world. As well as being delicious as smooth or crunchy peanut butter, their seeds are high in healthy fats and protein and can be pressed into oil.

phys-org.title: The best math lesson for children might be happening at your kitchen table, shows study
phys-org.description: In the minds of many people, math lives in the classroom—on blackboards, in textbooks, and in tests. New research from Amber Simpson, associate professor in the Department of Teaching, Learning, and Educational Leadership at Binghamton University's College of Community and Public Affairs, shows how math is happening all around us, especially at home, and that families don't even realize the role they play in how children experience mathematics.

phys-org.title: Green view index scores predict urban microbial diversity
phys-org.description: Researchers from the University of Helsinki, Natural Resources Institute Finland, Tamkang University and National Taiwan University investigated how the Green View Index (GVI) relates to the richness and diversity of bacteria in the Taipei metropolitan area in Taiwan. The more vegetation in the area, the richer its microbial community. The Green View Index measures visible greenery from the pedestrian perspective. The work is published in the journal Landscape and Urban Planning.

phys-org.title: Like humans, great apes think differently from each other
phys-org.description: For decades, scientists have been studying the cognition of great apes to understand how our own complex cognitive abilities evolved. Much of the research is based on the idea that if a particular ability—like using gestures to communicate—is found only in species that are closely related to us, then it's likely the trait appeared relatively late in our evolutionary history.

phys-org.title: Flexible cryogenic cables for dilution refrigerators could pave path to practical quantum computers
phys-org.description: By harnessing the unique properties of quantum mechanics, scientists and engineers worldwide seek to enable systems with extraordinary capabilities. Many of them are working on the highly anticipated development of quantum computers capable of completing complex calculations at unprecedented speeds. These computers could meet the growing computational demands of both scientific research and data-intensive industries like finance, cybersecurity, and medicine.

phys-org.title: 'Youniversalism' measures growing reliance on personal truth
phys-org.description: It has often been suggested that we now live in a "post-truth" world. People increasingly rely on their own feelings as a yardstick for what is true. Psychologists at the University of Amsterdam (UvA) have now developed the "Youniversalism" scale to allow them to measure people's belief in subjective and experiential truths. The research is published in the journal Personality and Individual Differences.

phys-org.title: Hidden mitochondrial genes emerge as mealybugs encode two genes on one DNA stretch
phys-org.description: What if a single sentence could carry two completely different meanings, one when read forward and another when read backward? In a new study, researchers at Arizona State University have discovered a biological version of this idea. Working with the mitochondria of a tiny insect called the citrus mealybug, the team found that the same stretch of DNA can carry two different genes—sets of genetic instructions used by the cell—with one encoded on each strand of the DNA's ladder-like structure

phys-org.title: Q&A: Why so many whales are in Vancouver waters—and how to (legally) spot them
phys-org.description: If you've noticed more whales visiting local waters, you're not imagining it: Vancouver's gargantuan guests are here thanks to the season, great grub and conservation successes, researchers say.

phys-org.title: Comb jelly embryos reveal embryonic signaling center shared across early animal evolution
phys-org.description: In order for vertebrate embryos to develop their body axes, they require what is known as an embryonic signaling center. This group of cells provides the instructions that determine where up and down, left and right, and front and back are. Biologists at Friedrich Schiller University Jena have now discovered that even cnidarians—which form the sister group to all other multicellular animals, according to current understanding—possess this fundamental coordinate system. The study is published in

phys-org.title: Lava planet has hydrogen-rich, active atmosphere
phys-org.description: It's 2158, and you're chugging away on your Ph.D. in planetary volcanology from the University of Utopia Planitia on Mars. Graduate students still get paid a sub-living wage, so you've been stuck eating freeze-dried ramen for the past three years. You've completed studying Jupiter's moon Io, but now you have to leave the solar system for a good exoplanet analog. phys-org.title: Helios quantum computer tops 99.9% fidelity rates for one- and two-qubit operations
phys-org.description: A public-private partnership in the Mountain West announced new results today that mark steady progress toward the Department of Energy's goal of fault-tolerant quantum computing, systems large and reliable enough to solve complex problems.

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17312v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models can arrive at the same answer through reasoning paths that are unstable, contradictory, or difficult to rank consistently -- a failure mode especially prevalent in multi-step deductive reasoning. Existing methods assess reliability primarily through output dispersion -- measuring how much sampled answers differ -- but this discards a complementary signal: whether the model can consistently rank competing reasoning candidates.

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17339v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech offers a uniquely informative window into health by simultaneously engaging neurological, motor, respiratory, and vocal systems. Current clinical speech AI methods have largely progressed through isolated condition-specific studies, making results difficult to compare and generalization difficult to assess. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17443v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming a major way for consumers to find products, but we do not yet understand how brands compete in this new channel. We study brand dynamics in LLM recommendations using skincare products -- a category where consumers cannot easily judge quality before buying and must rely on brand reputation -- across three commercial LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet, Gemini 3 Flash), with a robustness check on search goods.

arxiv-ai.description:

Abstract: Generative AI and large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to question generation and automated assessment. undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

public-dom.title: Louis Pope Gratacap, A Curator in Lost Worlds
public-dom.description: Arguably the first work of fiction to feature a *Tyrannosaurus rex*, Louis Pope Gratacap’s *The New Northland* (1915) is at once kaleidoscopic, mischievous, fascinating — and exhausting. Richard Fallon explores this “lost world” novel, finding a work as interested in cutting-edge science as it was in paying dues to its generic precursors.

public-dom.description: 69 images of kite flying from across 5 centuries and some 10 countries.

public-dom.description: Paintings from an era when Venetians brawled on bridges.

public-dom.title: Genevieve Stebbins’ Delsarte System of Dramatic Expression (1886)
public-dom.description: A philosophical system and a practical guide for the cultivation of dramatic genius.

public-dom.title: The Launch of Our Mid-Year Fundraiser!
public-dom.description: Our Mid-Year Fundraiser is launched, and the new postcards theme will be Soil.

public-dom.title: Covers from Cerîde-i Adliye, a Turkish Law Journal (1924–26)
public-dom.description: Legal infographics that reflect a Turkish nation in flux.

public-dom.title: Animal, Vegetable, Lamb: The Zoophyte from Tartary
public-dom.description: In the Middle Ages, rumours spread across Europe of a strange hybrid creature, half-animal, half-plant, known as the Vegetable Lamb of Tartary. A hoax based on fern rhizomes? A euphemism for culled fetal lambs? Or perhaps a medieval misapprehension of cotton? Thom Sliwowski traces the roots of this fabled zoophyte.

public-dom.title: Harold A. Taylor’s Autochromes of California Flowers (early 20th century)
public-dom.description: Photographs of flowers by an advocate of California’s beauty.

public-dom.title: The Prophecies of the Brahan Seer (1877)
public-dom.description: Historical predictions from the Scottish Nostradamus.

public-dom.title: “Plaything of the Gods”: Photographs of Pushball (early 1900s)
public-dom.description: Photographs and films of a forgotten pastime.

public-dom.title: Twilight of the Velocipede: Typesetting Races before the Age of Linotype
public-dom.description: Before Linotype revolutionised typesetting in the 1880s, compositors set texts by hand — and they set them *fast*. Alex Wright rediscovers the thrilling world of typesetting races, which drew crowds in the thousands, offered huge cash prizes, and helped women "Swifts" fight for workplace equity.

public-dom.title: Diagrams from Willem ten Rhijne’s De Acupunctura (1683)
public-dom.description: A Dutch physician’s encounter with acupuncture.

public-dom.title: Longitude by Way of Wounded Hounds: Kenelm Digby’s Sympathetick Powder (1669 edition)
public-dom.description: A treatise on a powder that can cure wounds at a distance.

public-dom.title: Pyramid of the Capitalist System (1911)
public-dom.description: The working class undergirds everything in this cartoon of capitalist society.

public-dom.title: Magic by Return of Post: How Mail Order Delivered the Occult
public-dom.description: What allowed occultism to blossom in the United States at the turn of the 20th century? Linotype machines, cheap pulp paper, and newly improved postal networks. Allan Johnson investigates the forgotten history and (still living) world of mail-order magic.

public-dom.title: Pulex irritans: The Attack of the Monster (1885)

public-dom.title: “A Beautiful Purplish Hue”: Frank Dudley Beane’s Experience with Ergot and Cannabis Indica (1884)
public-dom.description: An early contribution to drug literature, in which a man came to be fashioned out of wood.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.

proj-syn.title: White House Fight Night
proj-syn.description: The venue on the South Lawn for UFC Freedom 250 was built, approved, lit, filmed, defended, watched, and enjoyed as part of a celebration of freedom. President Donald Trump’s chosen object to represent that celebration was a cage.

proj-syn.title: The US-Iran Agreement Is a First Step
proj-syn.description: While the recently announced US-Iranian memorandum of understanding is certainly good news, it is not definitive. The path from a statement of diplomatic intent to a fully restored, non-inflationary energy supply chain is fraught with political, technical, and physical risks.

proj-syn.title: Developing-Country Risk Is Being Mispriced
proj-syn.description: When investors say there are no “bankable” projects in developing economies, they are typically referring less to project quality than to the cost of capital. But the assumptions driving up risk premia are not supported by the evidence, and until this changes, the misallocation of capital will continue to undermine development.

proj-syn.title: The Fed Has Been Honest and Stupid
proj-syn.description: It would be easy—and a mistake—to blame the US Federal Reserve’s many blunders on corrupt bureaucrats or imagined conspiracies. The truth of the matter is that the central bank relies on an outdated regional map and lagging indicators that no longer tell the whole story, while battling macroeconomic blazes that politicians stoke.

proj-syn.title: A New Framework for Climate Displacement
proj-syn.description: Global warming is already uprooting communities and impoverishing people who remain in vulnerable areas—a crisis that is often overshadowed by the focus on decarbonization. But the Global Climate Mobility Principles offer policymakers a framework for ensuring that these individuals maintain their agency and rights.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Is All About Lebanon Now
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump says that he "calls the shots" on negotiating with Iran, and Israel has no choice but to submit to a deal that undermines its security interests. But a deal that makes Trump the protector of Lebanon—and, by extension, Iran-backed Hezbollah—could put the US and Israel on a collision course.

proj-syn.title: Every British Prime Minister’s Nightmare
proj-syn.description: The true nature of Britain’s “special relationship” with the United States has far more to do with American financiers’ willingness to keep borrowing to purchase British government debt than with history, culture, or Britain’s defense needs. Every UK Prime Minister must bear this burden, which is rapidly becoming unsustainable.

proj-syn.title: India’s Unfinished Reform Agenda
proj-syn.description: Elevated oil prices, potentially strong El Niño conditions during the monsoon season, and the tariff-induced fragmentation of global trade are bearing down on the Indian economy and will likely be a drag on GDP growth. But these adverse conditions may be a blessing in disguise if they force India to complete its economic reform agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Middle East’s New Normal
proj-syn.description: The most likely outcome of the Iran war is not peace but an unsatisfying ceasefire that leaves the underlying issues unresolved. This will mean an uneasy equilibrium in which Gulf countries go their own way, US influence wanes, and the regional order remains unsettled.

proj-syn.title: No Bridge Over Healing Waters for the G7
proj-syn.description: The French G7 presidency’s focus on global imbalances is both welcome and problematic. While long-standing trade imbalances between the United States, Europe, and China are, if anything, becoming even more troublesome, the leaders’ summit in Évian-les-Bains will do nothing to address the problem.

proj-syn.title: Are Government Stakes the Key to AI Sovereignty?
proj-syn.description: At first glance, reports that the US and Chinese governments are both considering taking stakes in national AI champions would seem to suggest a convergence between the world’s two leading AI powers. But a closer look reveals stark differences in their underlying strategies.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: Jefferson’s Revolutionary Language
proj-syn.description: Of the delegates who assembled in Philadelphia in 1776 for the Second Continental Congress, only Thomas Jefferson possessed the skill, knowledge, and linguistic gifts to make the Declaration of Independence an immortal text. He was the self-appointed conscience of America, and sensational imagery was his stock-in-trade.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of the Enslaved
proj-syn.description: For African-Americans, the Declaration of Independence was nothing but a “thin veil to cover the crimes” of slavery, as Frederick Douglass put it. Inspired by Haiti’s Declaration of Independence, free and enslaved Black people in the US found themselves subverting America’s founding document to achieve their own emancipation.

proj-syn.title: Free-Market Capitalism Is Destroying US Democracy
proj-syn.description: Far from two sides of the same coin, free-market capitalism and democracy are fundamentally incompatible. The only way to restore US democracy is to transform the system, so that it compensates innovators but limits their market power, while ensuring that the benefits of economic progress are more equitably shared.
